title: Data Engineer
description:
Optus is an Australian telecommunications company, delivering more than 11 million services to our customers every day across mobile, broadband and digital solutions.
Network Analytics leads the development and maintenance of advanced analytics models using large-scale data and a big data ecosystem with AI/ML and ETL tools. The Data Engineer builds and manages high-quality, scalable data pipelines on cloud platforms like GCP, Azure, and AWS to support network performance and analytics. The role also involves close collaboration with stakeholders to uncover opportunities and drive business value from network data.
Your day to day will consist of
Design, build, and maintain end‑to‑end data pipelines for network data (telemetry, performance, fault, capacity, configuration).
Work with structured and semi‑structured data from network systems (e.g. OSS/BSS, monitoring platforms).
Develop scalable data transformations using SQL, Python, and Spark/PySpark, ensuring pipelines are reliable and performant.
Perform exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, and support analytical use cases like anomaly detection, forecasting, and optimisation.
Collaborate with data scientists/ML engineers to enable model training, deployment, and translate insights for stakeholders.
Build and operate cloud-based data solutions across GCP, Azure, and AWS using tools like Databricks, Kubernetes, and CI/CD practices.
Ensure strong data quality, governance, and compliance by implementing monitoring, resolving data issues, and managing metadata, lineage, and security.
What makes you perfect for the role
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Telecommunications, Engineering, or a related field, with 4+ years of relevant experience.
Proven experience building production-grade data pipelines and analytical solutions, ideally in telecommunications or network environments.
Hands-on expertise with cloud platforms (GCP, Azure, AWS) and distributed processing tools like Spark/Databricks.
Strong technical skills in SQL, Python, and knowledge of network concepts and KPIs (performance, fault, capacity, availability).
Understanding of data quality frameworks, governance principles, and modern cloud-native architectures (CI/CD, containerisation).
Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and results-oriented mindset with the ability to plan and deliver effectively.
What’s in it for you?
Competitive remuneration and employee discounts. Make life easier (and more affordable) with $80 monthly credit and 25% off Optus products and unique shopping discounts with our retail partners.
Competitive leave policies, including additional 'Connected’ days to focus on culture, family, health, community, or whatever’s important to you.
We support growing families with inclusive, carer-neutral paid Parental Leave of up to 16 weeks.
Direct your own development and build future-ready skills with Optus U’s industry-focused micro-credentials, developed with La Trobe and Macquarie Universities.
Build meaningful connections through employee-led networks and diversity initiatives including Culture Connect, Elevate Women, Disability Network and Express Yourself (LGBTQIA+).

This position is offered on a fixed-term, 12-month contract.

Salary Packaging benefits up to $15,899 per annum.

Data Engineering & Architecture
Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines to support the AAEH AtoZ database and associated systems.
Develop and manage data integration processes across multiple internal and external data sources.
Ensure data quality, integrity, and consistency across platforms.

Develop and maintain data models, data warehouses, and data lakes to support reporting and analytics.
Optimise data storage and retrieval processes for performance and scalability.
Support integration with Microsoft data technologies and platforms where applicable.

Monitor data pipelines and troubleshoot issues to ensure platform reliability.
Establish best practices for data lifecycle management.
Reporting & Insights Enablement
Support analytics and reporting capabilities by preparing curated datasets for dashboards and visualisation tools.
Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure data supports operational and strategic decision-making.
Documentation & Continuous Improvement
Maintain technical documentation, including data models, pipelines, and architecture.
Continuously improve data processes, performance, and reliability.
The successful candidate will have:
Tertiary qualifications in Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience (typically 3–5+ years) in data engineering or a similar role.
Strong experience building and maintaining data pipelines and working with large datasets.
Proficiency in SQL and experience with data modelling and database design.
Experience with ETL/ELT processes and modern data architectures.
Familiarity with cloud-based data platforms and tools.
Experience preparing data for reporting and analytics (e.g. Power BI or similar tools).
Strong problem-solving skills with attention to data quality and detail.
Experience with version control and development practices (e.g. Git, CI/CD pipelines).
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
Experience working in Agile environments.

Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work across multidisciplinary teams.

For Workforce Management, this means leading one of our most critical parts of our product, owning the evolution of our scalable, cloud-native architectures, and ensuring we continue to deliver world-class solutions trusted by thousands of organisations worldwide. 
AI at Humanforce 
At Humanforce, we’re not experimenting at the edges of AI, we’re redesigning the core of how we operate. We see AI as a fundamental shift, not an incremental improvement, and we’re deliberately moving toward becoming an AI-native organisation. 
That means rethinking how work gets done end-to-end, how we build our products, make decisions, serve customers, and scale impact. We’re not layering AI onto old ways of working, we’re redefining and reimagining our processes, tools, and team structures to take full advantage of what AI makes possible. 
This is a moment of real change. We’re moving fast, learning in real time, and challenging assumptions about roles, workflows, and productivity. If you’re motivated by transformation, not optimisation, and want to help shape how a global tech company operates in an AI-first future, Humanforce is the place to do it. 
Who you are 
As a Senior Data Engineer, You'll have full ownership of our infrastructure and deployment architecture, from ClickHouse cluster administration through to IaC and CI/CD. You'll set the technical direction for the data engineering function and partner with our Data Engineer, Data Analyst, DBA, Software Engineers, and Product to deliver a reliable, scalable, and observable platform. The bulk of your ownership sits on the infrastructure and platform layer, though strong dbt and analytics engineering instincts will accelerate your impact.
This isn't a typical data engineering role. The platform is customer-facing, data and infrastructure you build and secure is consumed directly by end users across a multi-tenanted SaaS product, where performance and security are non-negotiable.
What you will do 
Own end-to-end data infrastructure: Terraform provisioning, AWS architecture, and all ClickHouse cluster administration (replication, sharding, performance tuning, schema governance).
Lead the design and implementation of multi-tenant row-level security within ClickHouse, coordinating with the application layer.
Own and evolve the CI/CD architecture for infrastructure and transformation pipelines (GitHub Actions).

We’re hipages, Australia’s #1 digital platform connecting homeowners with trusted tradies. As an ASX-listed tech company, we're on a mission to transform the trade industry and improve lives.
With teams across Australia, New Zealand, the Philippines and Vietnam, we work as one team with a shared purpose.
We’re proud to be a certified
Great Place to Work and WORK180’s #1 Employer for Women. At hipages, you’ll find real impact, career growth and a workplace where everyone belongs.
About the role
As a Data Scientist, you will be supporting hipages through data-driven insights and enabling the business through both data capabilities and advanced application of data to business problems. Your role contributes to the development and execution of hipages' commercial strategy.
You will be influential in supporting the hipages marketplace as we continue to evolve and apply your experience to find the best experience for our customers. You’ll design and deploy machine learning applications as well as leverage hipages’ data assets to discover insights and shape the product experience.
Why join us?
Hybrid working model
In-house Talent Development team to prioritise personal and career growth
Competitive salary, benefits and perks
Cross-functional collaboration
Hands-on learning opportunities and workshops for continuous upskilling
How you will add value
Analyse data, trends, and results, as well as translate into business impact for stakeholders and recommendations for product enhancements
Analyse the acquisition funnel to uncover insights and opportunities that drive jobs and tradie growth
Contribute to growing our user base by supporting segmentation strategies to build a customised consumer experience
Design, implement, launch and measure experiments to test new products and packages
Identify new commercial opportunities for advanced analytics within the organisation, leveraging AI/ML to drive growth
Identify commercial opportunities leveraging large and/or complex, internal and external data assets
About you
Passionate about all things data, and the ability to digest complex data and storytelling
Hands-on experience with A/B testing for SaaS products
Experience in classical machine learning
Experience working with enterprise data warehouses
Advanced proficiency in Python and strong SQL skills
Great communication skills with the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive strategic outcomes
Life at hipages
We’re more than just a workplace. We’re a place where you can be yourself, do great work and grow your career. Recognised as a Great Place to Work, our inclusive, supportive culture helps people thrive.
You’ll use the best tools and tech, with real impact on our products and customers. We invest in your development and lead with coaching, not micromanagement – it’s why 85% of our team say their leader is great.
And there’s more:
Diverse, collaborative teams that love solving problems
Agile squads, hackathons, off-sites and roadshows
Extra leave for birthdays, volunteering, and more
Healthy snacks, continental breakfast and fresh fruit
Sydney CBD office near Town Hall and Gadigal Stations
Tailored growth support, mentoring and stretch projects
A vibrant social scene - we work hard and have fun doing it
We prioritise Diversity
At hipages, innovation and collaboration thrive in diverse and inclusive teams. We don’t expect you to know everything - we care more about who you are as a person, a team member, and a leader.
We’re proud to be endorsed by WORK180 for supporting women’s careers and we value diversity across culture, age, gender identity and sexual orientation.
Research shows that men often apply when they meet just 60% of the criteria, while women and minority groups wait until they tick every box. If you think you’d be a great fit - even if you don’t meet every requirement- we’d love to hear from you.
We’re also a Circle Back Initiative Employer, which means we commit to responding to every applicant.

title: Associate Data Scientist
description:
If you live in Australia or New Zealand, you've likely heard of AMP. But at a time when society is changing, we are too. We're now a nimbler business with new leadership and thinking.
For us, these are exciting times. There's a real potential for big thinkers to help us redefine what financial services could be. And turn our legacy into something even more positive and powerful for the future.
Help people create their tomorrow, while you create yours
We help people with their banking, super, retirement and finances. Through upturns, downturns, recessions, and major life transitions. Every day, we help people see and make more of their financial potential, so that they can create their tomorrow. And we've been doing it for over 170 years.
If we do our job well, we genuinely add to the prosperity of our country and its people.
This role sits within the Bank Data Sciences team and works closely with a wide range of stakeholders across AMP Bank. You'll collaborate with teams including lending, marketing, and customer retention to build, enhance, and maintain data‑driven tools and platforms that support both frontline decision‑making and customer outcomes.
As a Data Scientist, you'll apply data science and analytics techniques within the banking and finance environment, with a strong focus on home lending. The role involves analysing data using R, Python, and SQL, developing and maintaining R Shiny applications, and translating complex data into clear insights that inform strategy and enable smarter business decisions.
How will you make an impact
Design, develop, deploy, and maintain R Shiny applications and analytics solutions that support business decision‑making, operational efficiency, and customer outcomes.
Analyse complex datasets and develop predictive models using R, Python, and SQL to generate actionable insights, optimise processes, and support pricing strategies aligned to portfolio growth.
Collaborate with cross‑functional teams including Finance, Product, Risk, Marketing, and Lending to understand business needs and deliver data‑driven solutions.
Develop and maintain data pipelines, SQL queries, and automated workflows to support data extraction, processing, reporting, and model performance monitoring.
Clearly communicate insights and recommendations to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders, continuously refining and improving analytics solutions over time.
What you will bring to the role
Bachelor's degree in data science, Actuarial Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
2-4 years' experience in data science or advanced analytics roles.
Strong capability in R (preferred), Python, and SQL for data analysis, modelling, and automation.
Hands‑on experience designing and deploying R Shiny applications.
Solid foundations in data manipulation, visualisation, and statistical analysis, using programming tools and/or Microsoft Excel.
Exposure to cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP for data processing or deployment.
Experience using version control tools (e.g. Git) and working within agile delivery environments.
Who you are
You're naturally curious, thoughtful in your approach and enjoy solving problems that make a real business impact. You're comfortable working through ambiguity, take ownership of your work and bring exceptional judgement, critical thinking and attention to detail to everything you do.
You're also an excellent communicator and collaborative team player, able to explain complex ideas clearly to different audiences. You work well with others, manage multiple priorities with confidence, and thrive in fast‑paced environments where teamwork, learning, and continuous improvement are valued.
Why we think you'll love working at AMP
Doing what we've always done is not an option, so your clever ideas will get airtime here. You'll be encouraged to speak up and try new things. If they don't work, we move on - better for it.
We know there's no one way of doing things. So, you won't have to sacrifice who you are or how you work to fit in here. We're inclusive and flexible in many of the ways you'd expect. And in some of the ways you wouldn't. As long as your health and wellbeing come first - at home and at work.
In fact, most of what makes AMP such a welcoming, enjoyable place to work are our people. Wherever you go, you'll find moments to connect, feel valued and do meaningful work.
Whether it's through our first‑class leaders who are invested in you and your success. Through year‑round opportunities to volunteer, fundraise and give back to the community. Or in the everyday challenges you face as we work together to strengthen this great organisation. Challenges that will stretch you, amplify your potential and compound the impact you have.
We believe in the power of inclusion and diversity. We're dedicated to fostering inclusion, diversity, and a warm feeling of belonging at AMP. It sparks creativity, ignites innovation, and turns up the dial on the quality of our decisions and performance. This not only makes our workplace more engaged, but also leads to better connections with our customers.
We're your allies in the search for the perfect fit - when you apply, let us know how we can support you to put your best self forward during our selection process.
We're also committed to enhancing employment opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, so we enthusiastically encourage candidates from these backgrounds to apply and explore our Reconciliation Plan on our website.
Ready to create your tomorrow?
If you're someone who sees opportunity where others see challenge, come and work with us in smart, progressive ways as we transform an iconic Australian brand for the future. And, through a series of career‑defining moments, create your own tomorrow.
Don't procrastinate! We review applications when we get them, and if we discover the ideal candidate, we may close the role earlier than the advertised close date.
Looking forward to meeting you.

title: Data Scientist, AI
description:
Hello. We’re Virgin Australia. We’re the airline that’s always done things a little different. Our way. The Virgin way. We’re on a mission to make flying better than ‘nice’. And to do that, it takes a team of talented people who are passionate about customer experience, doing the right thing always, with a focus on safety – in the air, on the ground and in our workplaces. A team who values real diversity and inclusion, in a big brand with big ambitions.

As a Data Scientist (AI), you’ll join a growing AI team that is helping shape the future of Virgin Australia.
This is an exciting opportunity to work on greenfield AI initiatives that are strategically aligned to the business and focused on taking AI solutions from concept through to production. You'll sit at the intersection of data science, software engineering and AI, applying cutting-edge techniques to solve real business problems across customer experience, operational efficiency and employee productivity.
We're looking for an engineer-scientist hybrid who is passionate about generative AI and enjoys turning emerging technologies into practical, scalable solutions. You'll work closely with engineers, product teams and business stakeholders to design, evaluate and improve AI systems that deliver measurable outcomes.
In this role, you will:
Design, build and optimise production AI solutions leveraging LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic workflows and tool integration patterns
Develop and maintain AI data pipelines, embeddings, knowledge stores and retrieval systems
Create evaluation frameworks and testing approaches for non-deterministic AI systems

You’ll be great in this role if you have…
Hands-on experience with LLMs, RAG architectures, agentic systems, tool/function calling and retrieval workflows.
Strong Python development skills and a solid foundation in software engineering practices.
Experience designing evaluation frameworks for AI systems and measuring solution quality.
Knowledge of embeddings, vector search, agent planning and retrieval optimisation techniques.
Experience working with AI orchestration frameworks such as Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK or similar.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work across technical and business stakeholders
Desirable
Experience with Databricks, MLflow, AWS and modern data ecosystems.
Experience with vector databases and search technologies such as pgvector, OpenSearch or equivalent.
Exposure to observability, monitoring and evaluation tooling for AI systems.
Knowledge of LLMOps, AgentOps and MLOps practices.
Experience with API integrations, scheduled pipelines and production deployments.
Understanding of security, privacy and responsible AI principles.
Open-source contributions or formal study in generative AI, NLP or machine learning.
Why join us?
You'll be joining Virgin Australia at a pivotal point in our AI journey, working on some of the organisation's most strategically important initiatives.
This is an opportunity to be part of a growing AI team that is building production-ready AI solutions at scale. You'll have the freedom to explore emerging technologies, contribute to technical direction and help shape how AI is adopted across one of Australia's most recognised brands.
We’re committed to looking after you, with some of the best benefits and conditions in the industry – including (but not limited to):
Discounted flights for you and your loved ones (including $1000 worth of travel credits per year)
A flexible, hybrid work style. Work from home or the office, adapt your location to suit your style and needs
One of Brisbane’s most admired head office locations, with South Bank train station, a supermarket, pharmacy, and lunch options downstairs plus a 5-minute walk to the Busway, a rooftop restaurant and onsite gym (with a low membership fee) and South Bank Parklands just across the road
Discounts on travel insurance, lounge membership, car hire, accommodation, and experiences worldwide
Cheaper hospitality, retail, technology, beauty and wellness services
Free counselling and access to a well-being app to support your physical, mental, social and financial health
‘Dress for Your Day’ – enjoy the freedom to wear whatever makes you feel great for the type of work you do and the day you have ahead of you
When everyone is included, everyone wins
We’re all individuals. And we love that. That’s why we encourage applications from Indigenous Australians, people with disability, those from diverse cultural backgrounds, our friends in the LGBTQIA+ community, and anyone else who wants to join our family.
Ready to apply?
We’re ready to hear from you. Apply now.

title: Research Associate - Data Scientist in Ecosystem Science
description:
One of Australia’s leading research & teaching universities
Vibrant campus life with a strong sense of community & inclusion
Enjoy a career that makes a difference by collaborating & learning from the best
At UNSW, we pride ourselves on being a workplace where the best people come to do their best work.
The School of Biological, Earth and Environmental Sciences is a large, collaborative and multi-disciplinary school in the Faculty of Science at the University of New South Wales with over 170 academic, research and professional staff. In 2025, the school obtained $22M in research funding, produced over 800 scientific publications and is frequently rated among the top schools across UNSW in student experience surveys. Level A ($113k - $121k) plus 17% Superannuation and annual leave loading

Contribute to documentation, elaboration of case studies and example applications.

title: Product Data Scientist
description:
At Fitness Passport, we are driven by a clear purpose — to make fitness more accessible, so more people can lead active and healthier lives. Established in 2006, we’re a corporate health and fitness program partnering with the public sector, corporate employers, and leading fitness facilities across Australia and New Zealand, providing members with access to a wide range of gyms and wellness resources.
As we enter an exciting new phase of growth, Fitness Passport is executing an ambitious strategy while keeping our member experience a top priority.
The Role
We're looking for a curious, commercially minded data professional to join our Data team as a Product Decision Scientist (PDS). This is our most business-facing data role — you'll embed directly into a product squad, learn how that part of the business works, and use data to help it perform better.
You'll spend 60–80% of your time working alongside Product Managers, GMs, and Software Engineers within your aligned squad, while staying connected to the broader Data team. Whether it's dashboards, deep-dive analyses, experiments, or predictive models — you'll reach for whatever tool the problem needs.
What you will be doing:
Build and maintain dashboards for your aligned squad. If a dashboard is wrong, stale, or confusing you are empowered and expected to fix it.
Take a business question, scope the analytical work, do the analysis, and deliver a clear answer.
Write PRs for the AEs to review to enhance our shared DBT project, especially in areas closely related to your squad.
Build models where they’re useful — churn prediction, revenue forecasting, pricing analysis. Have the judgement to know when such a model will add value and when it won’t.
Act as the go-to data partner for your squad's Product Manager and GM — helping them make better decisions, faster
Translate commercial questions into analytical work, and translate findings back into clear recommendations
About You
Genuinely curious and passionate about health, wellness, and fitness.
Solid foundation of SQL with an understanding of window functions, join logic, CTEs, and query performance
Python or R for statistical analysis, modelling, and reproducible analytical work.
Data visualisation skills using a BI tool (current tool is power BI)
Can design and run experiments with appropriate statistical rigour — knows when results are significant and when they’re noise.
Familiar enough with dbt and Git to contribute to the shared modelling layer via PR. You don’t need to be an expert, but you should feel comfortable contributing this way.
Picks up ambiguous problems and figures them out without needing a detailed requirement specification
Strong commercial acumen, you connect the dots between data and revenue — understanding how your work drives real business outcomes.
What You’ll Love
Fitness Passport is officially a Great Place to Work — again!
We’re proud of our culture, and even prouder of the people who make it what it is.
At Fitness Passport, we’re not just about providing access to great gyms and wellness facilities — we’ve also created a fantastic place to work. Our company values of Collaboration, Growth, Respect, Integrity and Wellbeing define our culture and the principles we use to operate our business.
We don’t just talk about wellness - we live it! Our BeneFit Passport Rewards Program and values-driven culture support your well-being inside and outside of work.
Here’s what’s waiting for you:
Your very own Fitness Passport membership – access thousands of fitness facilities because we believe in what we offer
3 paid well-being days per year – because rest and recharge matter
Hybrid & flexible work – our Sydney-based team enjoys three days a week in our new head office
Generous WFH allowance to support our hybrid model
Ongoing wellness perks – think fitness challenges, guest speakers, and more
Paid parental leave to support you and your family
Mental health support through Clear Head & our Employee Assistance Program
Rewards & recognition – Earn Hero Points and get rewarded for your impact!

title: Data Scientist | Model & AI Risk
description:
Our Model Risk Management team provides independent oversight and challenge of model and AI risks are well managed across Macquarie globally. We assess whether models and AI systems are fit for purpose, appropriately controlled, and aligned to the firm’s risk appetite and to regulatory expectations. The team plays a critical role in enabling safe adoption of models and AI by providing robust validation, clear challenge and sound risk-based decisions.
At Macquarie, our advantage is bringing together diverse people and empowering them to shape all kinds of possibilities. We are a global financial services group operating in 31 markets and with 56 years of unbroken profitability. You’ll be part of a friendly and supportive team where everyone - no matter what role - contributes ideas and drives outcomes.
What role will you play?
As a Data Scientist within Model Risk Management, you will independently review, challenge and validate artificial intelligence use cases across the firm. Your work will assess whether AI systems are fit‑for‑purpose, operate as intended and ensure that the risks introduced are understood, appropriately controlled, and remain within the Macquarie’s risk appetite.
You will design and execute proportionate validation approaches, assess data, methodology, assumptions, and outcomes, and clearly articulate findings to technical and non‑technical stakeholders. Your analysis and judgement will directly inform model approvals, usage decisions, and risk acceptance.
Working closely with, but independently from, model developers, product owners, and business stakeholders, you will provide constructive challenge that enables safe and sustainable AI adoption. You will also contribute to the evolution of AI validation practices, tooling and standards within the team, sharing knowledge and strengthening collective capability.
What You Offer
A courageous mindset and a demonstrated track record of self‑directed learning, with the curiosity and discipline to stay ahead of rapidly evolving AI techniques and risks
Attention to detail and a knack for identifying problems
Experience developing or independently reviewing and validating artificial intelligence, machine learning, or statistical models
Strong programming capability in Python, R, or SQL, with experience interrogating large and complex datasets
Familiarity with modern AI techniques, including large language models, their limitations, failure modes, and associated risks
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts and risk trade‑offs clearly to both technical and senior non‑technical stakeholders
A structured, analytical, and sceptical mindset, with the ability to form independent judgement to make sound, commercial decisions balancing risks and rewards and to prioritise work in a collaborative environment.
We love hearing from anyone inspired to build a better future with us, if you're excited about the role or working at Macquarie we encourage you to apply.

Benefits
At Macquarie, you’re empowered to shape a career that’s rewarding in all the ways that matter most to you. Macquarie employees can access a wide range of benefits which, depending on employment type, include:
1 wellbeing leave day per year

Our Risk Management Group works as an independent, and centralised function, responsible for independent and objective review and challenge, oversight, monitoring and reporting in relation to Macquarie’s material risks. We are a global team that aims to manage the risks of today and anticipate the risks of tomorrow. Our divisions include compliance, credit, financial crime risk, market risk, operational risk, aggregate risk and prudential, and central.

description:

A critical part of this role involves partnering with engineering, research, and security operations to turn data science work into production defences that stand up against real attackers.
We are looking for a hands-on data scientist to help shape the predictive detection capabilities within Account Intelligence and the way we tell legitimate users apart from adversaries. While your focus may shift from time to time, you are expected to remain technical and hands on across the full model lifecycle, from exploring data and building models through to evaluating how your work performs once adversaries start adapting. You will be supported by experienced engineering and research teams to take your work from notebook to production.
What You Will Be Doing
Build predictive defences: Use data and models to support the development of risk mitigation strategies and interventions while preserving and improving the user experience, building, training, and iterating on predictive models that stand up to real adversaries at Kasada scale.
Evaluate rigorously: Pressure test your own work before anyone else has to. Evaluate model performance and trade-offs carefully, so detection decisions stand up to scrutiny from engineering, product, and security operations long after the model goes live.
Partner with engineering, research, and product: Work alongside engineers, researchers, and product managers to take models from notebook to production, integrating them into Kasada's platform and iterating on them as customer needs and attacker behaviour shift.
Make models legible: Make your models and their outputs understandable to both technical and non-technical colleagues. Detection decisions should never be a black box to the teams that rely on them, and that bar sits with you.
Hunt adversarial patterns: Analyse large datasets to surface anomalies, identify adversarial behaviours, and flag emerging attack patterns. Stay current with developments in adversarial ML and cybersecurity, and apply relevant techniques to strengthen our defence capabilities.
What You'll Bring
You're genuinely curious about fraud and the adversarial landscape, and you ask the right questions about attacker behaviour, false positives, and the real-world impact your models have on legitimate users
You enjoy partnering across engineering, research, and product, and you know how to explain models and their limitations to teammates and stakeholders who don't share your technical background
You have 2+ years of professional experience in data science or applied ML, with a solid foundation in statistical concepts, sampling, time-series data, and hands-on predictive modelling (e.g., gradient boosted trees, random forests, deep learning)
Proficiency in Python, SQL, and standard ML libraries (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow)
Experience evaluating predictive models in production or production-like settings, including thinking through precision, recall, calibration, and how models behave as attackers adapt
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with a keen attention to detail and a bias toward pressure testing your own work before shipping
Experience working within cloud environments (like AWS)
Additional bonus points if:
You have prior experience in fraud, trust and safety, account takeover, or abuse detection
You've built or supported ML models in adversarial settings, where attackers actively try to evade or retool against your defences

AWS, Clickhouse
Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow

description:
About Buildkite
Buildkite's CI platform is trusted by the world's leading engineering teams, shipping software to over 1,000,000,000 daily users.
Job Overview
We're hiring a Staff Engineer (ML) to join our Test Engine team. In this role, you'll define and lead the technical strategy for machine learning within Test Engine — specifically, building the models and infrastructure behind predictive test selection: using code changes to determine which tests actually need to run.
Staff Engineers at Buildkite are hands-on technical leaders. You'll influence how we design, build, and scale systems while supporting other engineers to deliver their best work. You'll be the most senior ML practitioner in the company, setting the technical direction for how we approach test selection and establishing the patterns and infrastructure that the broader ML effort builds on.
🔧 About the Team
The Test Engine team helps engineering teams ship faster by giving them visibility and control over their test suites. Today, that means real-time flaky test detection and management, intelligent test splitting across parallel jobs, and performance analytics and tracing — all working across any CI/CD platform, not just Buildkite Pipelines.
Test Engine already ingests billions of test runs. We have deep visibility into test suites, codebases, and the relationships between them. The next step is using that data to answer a fundamental question: for a given code change, which tests are most likely to fail?
We believe the industry is moving away from running full test suites on every change. The teams that can shift their outer testing loop into a fast, precise inner loop — running only the tests that matter — will ship value to their customers dramatically faster. For many of our customers, that speed is existential. Switching costs are low, competition is fierce, and the teams with faster feedback loops win.
This is where ML comes in. If we can model the relationship between code changes and test failures, we can give engineering teams a fundamentally faster development cycle. We're not trying to optimise individual tests — we're trying to build a generalised solution to test selection that works across codebases, frameworks, and languages.
🚀 What You'll Do
Own Technical Direction for ML in Test Engine
Lead and define the ML strategy for predictive test selection — from early experimentation through to models running reliably in production at scale
Lead the technical investigation into how we build a generalised test selection model, and shape the approach based on what the data tells you
Lead the design of the ML architecture end-to-end: feature engineering from code changes and test history, model training and evaluation, serving infrastructure, and feedback loops for continuous improvement
Drive key decisions around model operationalisation — latency constraints (test selection has to be fast enough to sit in the critical path), prediction accuracy trade-offs, and graceful degradation when confidence is low
Shape how ML capabilities integrate with Test Engine's existing data infrastructure — billions of ingested test runs, test-to-code mapping, and the intelligent splitting engine
Build and Scale the ML Platform
Build the ML platform layer so that getting a model into production is fast and repeatable
Design, build, and maintain the data pipelines that feed ML workloads — connecting code change signals with test execution history at scale
Train, evaluate, and deploy models, taking ownership through to monitoring and retraining in production
Instrument production models with observability metrics: prediction accuracy, latency, coverage, false negative rates, and drift detection
Solve the hardest technical challenges at the intersection of code analysis and test data — feature extraction from diffs, generalisation across languages and frameworks, and handling the cold-start problem for new tests and repositories
Lead and Unblock
Investigate and resolve complex performance and reliability issues across the data and ML stack
Share knowledge and drive engineering best practices across teams through documentation, mentorship, and pairing
Support the wider engineering organisation by contributing to cross-team tooling, infrastructure, and frameworks
Communicate trade-offs effectively and build alignment around technical decisions
Work closely with customers to understand how test selection fits into their development workflows, and ensure the product delivers real impact
🎨 Skills & Experience We Value
Technical Expertise
Deep proficiency in Python, with strong experience building production ML systems end-to-end
Proven experience designing and operating ML infrastructure at scale — model registries, feature stores, serving layers, experiment tracking, or similar
Strong experience with data processing at scale — whether batch or streaming frameworks (Spark, Flink, or similar)

Comfort working in cloud environments (AWS) and with containerised workloads (Docker, Kubernetes)
In short, we'd expect equal comfort and high level capability in the end to end process from designing and building models through to deploying them.

Full-time

Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Where and how you can work
Our flagship campus is in Sydney, with a second campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, and Auckland, NZ. You have flexibility in how and where you work — whether that’s from one of our spaces, from home, or a mix of both. This role is remote‑friendly within Australia, so you can choose the setup that empowers you and your team to do your best work.
About the team
We aim to build the world’s richest Ecosystem of apps for visual design and communications that supercharge Canva’s ability to meet the diverse needs of a billion users and drive Canva’s MAU growth.
With the proliferation of innovations in generative AI and as large organizations have increasingly complex workflows to manage their designs, Canva is well poised to become the platform that simplifies access and discovery of services related to visual design. We are already working with hundreds of developers to enable access to these exciting products with our Apps SDK and Canva public REST API!
As one of the groups in Ecosystem, the Integrations and Solutions Group builds Canva's AI integration layer — the infrastructure that connects Canva’s design capabilities to the world’s leading AI assistants. Our teams own the MCP platform, AI‑optimised tools and APIs, evaluation frameworks, and the agent architecture that powers millions of AI‑driven design interactions. We work directly with partners like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and we’re in the middle of a strategic shift from protocol‑first integrations toward intelligent, Canva‑hosted design agents.
As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll play a critical role in defining how AI platforms experience Canva — driving the technical standards, evaluation frameworks, and architectural decisions that ensure our integrations are reliable, measurable, and evolving with a rapidly changing ecosystem.
What you’d be doing in this role
As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that’s all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you’ll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.
At the moment, this role is focused on:
Drive the design and evolution of AI‑ready tools and APIs that enable LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others) to reliably interact with Canva’s design capabilities — defining the patterns and standards that other teams adopt for tool descriptions, payload structures, and intent‑based interfaces. Pioneer agent‑to‑agent communication approaches.
Own and evolve evaluation frameworks that systematically measure tool‑use accuracy across platforms — defining what “good” looks like for proxy‑based fast evals and real‑client production evals, and ensuring these frameworks scale as we add platforms and capabilities.
Shape Canva’s agent architecture — making strategic technical decisions about where intelligence should live (in external LLMs vs Canva‑hosted agents), building the orchestration layers that allow third‑party providers to invoke Canva’s design tools at scale, and driving automation of complex workflows like marketing campaigns.
Define and build observability systems that give multiple teams visibility into how AI assistants consume Canva’s tools in production — identifying failure patterns, setting quality benchmarks, and closing the loop between production data and continuous improvement.
Work across team and platform boundaries — proactively identifying problems not yet defined, understanding behavioural quirks across LLM platforms, and driving solutions that span the AI Integrations, API Capabilities, and Workflow Integrations teams.
Influence integration strategy with AI partners and internal teams — contributing to technical direction with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and shaping how Canva’s broader engineering organisation builds for AI consumption.
You're probably a match if
You’ve shipped LLM‑powered systems into production and can quantify your impact — things like improving tool‑call accuracy from X% to Y%, reducing agent error rates, cutting latency by Z%, or measurably improving user outcomes through better AI integration. We care about results, not just launches.
You proactively find and solve problems others haven’t defined yet — you’ve identified gaps in how LLMs consume tools or APIs, scoped the problem across teams, and driven the fix without waiting for someone to hand you a brief.
You’ve built or owned evaluation pipelines end‑to‑end — designing metrics, building benchmarking infrastructure, and using data to make architectural decisions about AI integrations at scale.
You set technical standards that others follow — whether that’s tool design patterns, API contracts for AI agents, documentation quality, or observability practices. Your work becomes the reference point.
You can connect external ecosystem changes to internal strategy — when a new LLM capability drops or a partner shifts their architecture, you can quickly assess the implications for Canva and re‑prioritise accordingly.
You’re proficient in Python and familiar with ML frameworks, and equally comfortable working with TypeScript/Node.js and cloud infrastructure (Cloudflare Workers, AWS, or similar).
You thrive in cross‑team, partner‑facing work — influencing engineering, product, and external AI platform teams to shape integration strategy. You’re comfortable operating across team boundaries without formal authority.
You’re energised by ambiguity and pace — the AI ecosystem is evolving rapidly, and you bring clarity and momentum rather than waiting for direction.
Don’t tick all the boxes? Don’t worry about that - nobody does!
We’d still love to hear from you! At Canva, we know that great engineers come from a variety of backgrounds, and we value passion, curiosity, and a willingness to learn just as much as specific experience. If you’re excited about this role but don’t tick every box, we encourage you to apply, you might a great fit in ways you didn’t expect!
What's in it for you?
Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you’ll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

As an AI Engineer, you will lead the experimentation, prototyping and deployment of advanced AI and Generative AI solutions that support client pursuits, industry demonstrations and scalable sector offerings. Working with leading foundation models and orchestration frameworks, you will translate emerging capabilities into practical, commercially viable solutions.
Within the AI Labs Engine Room, you will operate across enterprise-grade environments, advanced tooling and significant model and compute capacity, enabling experimentation and iteration at scale within secure enterprise guardrails.
You will combine rapid innovation with production discipline, leading engineers from concept to working solution at pace, shaping reusable AI accelerators and maturing successful prototypes into scalable enterprise deployments.
You will play a key role in shaping AI positioning across priority sectors and strategic accounts.
This role is based in Warrang - Sydney. This role can be performed from any of our EY offices across Australia. Our roles can potentially be adjusted to work flexibly with reduced hours. Please speak with us about potential options.
Your key responsibilities
Lead the prototyping and deployment of AI and Generative AI solutions supporting client pursuits and scalable sector offerings.
Architect and implement LLM-powered applications and agentic workflows, including multi-agent orchestration and advanced tool/function calling patterns.
Design and oversee data-driven architectures across cloud and hybrid environments.
Engineer scalable AI systems with embedded Responsible AI, governance and security controls.
Establish and embed MLOps and LLMOps practices including lifecycle management, experimentation tracking (MLflow, Weights & Biases), monitoring and safe deployment.
Design and optimise data pipelines integrating structured and unstructured data sources.
Select and implement vector database strategies alongside relational and NoSQL systems.
Deploy and optimise AI workloads across AWS, Azure or GCP using containerisation, CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code.
Mentor and guide junior engineers within the Engine Room.
Evaluate emerging models, orchestration approaches and low-code platforms to continuously strengthen EY's AI capability.
Skills and attributes for success
You are an experienced hands-on AI engineer who thrives in fast-moving environments and is comfortable leading technical design and delivery.
You will bring:
Strong foundation in AI, machine learning and Generative AI with proven hands-on delivery experience.
Deep experience working with LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Llama or equivalent).
Strong experience with orchestration frameworks such as LangChain and agentic system design.
Demonstrated experience applying MLOps and LLMOps in production or near-production environments.
Strong data engineering capability and architectural decision-making experience.
Experience deploying and optimising AI workloads across AWS, Azure or GCP.
Advanced Python programming capability and strong software engineering discipline.
Strong understanding of Responsible AI, compliance and enterprise security guardrails.
Ability to lead technical discussions with architects, sector leaders and clients.
Ideally, you'll also have the skills and attributes below but don't worry if you don't tick all the boxes. We're interested in your aptitude, attitude and willingness to learn.
Experience leading AI solutions that support commercial pursuits or reusable sector offerings.
Experience mentoring engineers or leading technical workstreams.
Exposure to model evaluation frameworks and structured experimentation environments.
A degree in computer science, engineering, data science or related discipline.
What we offer you

title: AI Engineer
description:
Company Description
At NCS Australia, we believe in doing technology services better. Our commitment to quality, focus on people, and willingness to challenge traditional thinking set us apart. Our team brings this belief to life by partnering with our clients and communities to make tomorrow together.
We are committed to creating an environment that prioritises innovation, collaboration, and purposeful work. Our diverse team is empowered to make a meaningful impact with curiosity, creativity and resilience to shape better outcomes. Join us and accept the challenge of creating a better tomorrow.
Job Description
We’re hiring AI Engineers to design and deliver end-to-end AI/ML solutions using AWS and/or Azure. The role involves building and deploying machine learning models, developing data pipelines, and working closely with cross-functional teams to solve real business problems.
Design, develop, and deploy AI/ML solutions using AWS and/or Azure services, including building and optimising machine learning models for real-world applications. The role involves developing and maintaining data pipelines and ML workflows, collaborating with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into scalable AI solutions, and contributing to end-to-end delivery from experimentation to production. You will also ensure best practices in coding, testing, and MLOps, and for senior candidates, take on additional responsibilities such as solution design, stakeholder engagement, and mentoring junior engineers.
Qualifications
Strong experience in AI/ML Engineering, Data Engineering, or related fields
Hands-on experience with AWS and/or Azure AI ecosystem
Strong programming skills in Python and familiarity with ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn)
Experience building and deploying ML models and pipelines in production environments
Good understanding of cloud architecture, data engineering, and ML lifecycle
Nice to Have
Exposure to Generative AI / LLMs (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.)
Experience with MLOps, CI/CD pipelines, and model deployment practices
Background in consulting or client-facing delivery environments
Additional Information
Why join us: 
NCS Australia is where you can feel at home, nurturing your talents and skills as we make tomorrow together, one day at a time. Our benefits include paid parental leave, initiatives focused on your well-being and discounted health insurance. You will also enjoy discounts on various products and services and be regularly recognised and rewarded for high performance. We are committed to your career development through our Capability Fingerprint, industry and partner training programs, special interest groups, and an AI-driven learning platform. No matter where you are in your career, we offer meaningful work and opportunities for growth.
NCS Australia is an equal-opportunity employer, and we take pride in our commitment to valuing and supporting our people and the communities we serve.We are dedicated to attracting, retaining and developing our people regardless of gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability and age. Applications are encouraged from all sectors of the community and we strongly encourage applications from the Veterans, Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander community.
At NCS Australia, we are committed to supporting adjustments throughout the recruitment and selection process, as well as during employment. We actively support and encourage people with disability to apply. 
Agencies:
We’ve got this. We request that you do not contact NCS employees outside of the Talent Acquisition team. NCS exclusively accepts resumes from agencies on our preferred supplier panel through the NCS Agency Portal. Agencies that submit resumes must have a valid fee agreement and be assigned to the particular requisition by the Talent Acquisition team. Any resumes that are submitted outside of this process will become the sole property of NCS. If a candidate is hired outside of this process, no fee or payment will be given.
Work rights and background checks: 
To be eligible for a position with us, applicants will need to have valid work rights for Australia and be willing to undergo a comprehensive background checking process, including probity and police checks

title: Senior Machine Learning & Data Engineer
description:
Senior Machine Learning & Data Engineer
At Nanosonics, we're on a mission to improve patient safety globally through innovative infection prevention technologies. As we continue to expand our digital and connected product ecosystem, we're investing in the next generation of data and AI capabilities.
We're seeking a Senior Machine Learning & Data Engineer to play a key role in building and scaling our enterprise data platform and machine learning capabilities. This newly created role offers the opportunity to influence strategy, architecture, and technology decisions while delivering solutions that drive business value and future innovation.
About the Role
You will draw on your expertise to design, build, and optimise scalable data and machine learning platforms that support analytics, operational insights, connected products, and AI initiatives across the business.
Working closely with business stakeholders, engineers, and technology partners, you'll help establish the foundations for Nanosonics' data-driven future.
Key Responsibilities
Design and deliver secure, scalable, and reliable cloud-based data platforms and pipelines.
Build and optimise data products, curated datasets, and ML-ready data solutions.
Support machine learning initiatives through feature engineering, data preparation, and operationalisation.
Drive engineering excellence through automation, CI/CD, testing, and best-practice development standards.
Contribute to data architecture, governance, security, and privacy frameworks.
Partner with stakeholders to identify opportunities for innovation and deliver data-driven business outcomes.
Influence the strategic direction of Nanosonics' data and AI capabilities.
About You
You are a hands-on data engineering leader who combines strong technical expertise with commercial thinking and a passion for innovation.
You will bring:
Extensive experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms in AWS or similar cloud environments.
Strong expertise in Python, SQL, data modelling, and modern data engineering tools such as dbt, Snowflake, Airflow, Databricks, or equivalent.
Experience supporting machine learning and AI solutions in production environments.
Knowledge of data governance, security, privacy, and compliance requirements.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions.
Experience within healthcare, medtech, life sciences, or regulated environments will be highly regarded.
Why Join Nanosonics?
This is a rare opportunity to build and shape enterprise data and AI capabilities within a global healthcare technology company. You'll have the autonomy to influence decisions, work with leading technologies, and help drive innovation that ultimately improves patient outcomes around the world.
If you're excited by the opportunity to create meaningful impact through data, machine learning, and technology, we'd love to hear from you.
